description:
## Current Architecture Summary

The Artlab IDE is built with Vite and runs under a dev server (vite dev, port 5173). The production build is defined in vite.config.js as a multi-page app (input: index.html + solar-system.html) with manual chunks for three, tone, and gsap. All app JS is bundled by Vite into static assets. There is no server-side rendering, no Node.js API layer, and no server-side build steps at runtime.

The key external dependencies are:
- Monaco editor: loaded at runtime from cdn.jsdelivr.net (MONACO_CDN = https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/monaco-editor@0.50.0/min/vs/loader.js). Monaco uses its own AMD loader (require.config) to pull worker scripts and language bundles from the same CDN base URL. This is not bundled by Vite.
- JSZip: loaded at runtime from cdn.jsdelivr.net (JSZIP_CDN = https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/jszip@3.10.1/dist/jszip.min.js). Also not bundled.
- Vite dev server: currently serves the examples/ directory at /examples/<name>/<entry>. This is the central deployment gap (see below).

## What Already Works for Static Hosting

1. Vite build output is fully static: vite build produces dist/ containing HTML, JS chunks, and CSS with no server-side logic. vite preview confirms this works against the dist/ directory.

2. All npm dependencies (three, tone, gsap, @dimforge/rapier3d-compat, etc.) are bundled by Vite and included in dist/assets/.

3. Monaco CDN loading works from GitHub Pages HTTPS: jsdelivr.net CDN is HTTPS, has permissive CORS headers (Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *), and is routinely used from GitHub Pages. No issues expected.

4. JSZip CDN: same cdn.jsdelivr.net, same CORS situation. Works fine.

5. User-written code via blob URLs (PreviewPane.run()): works on any origin, including GitHub Pages. import(blobURL) is permitted when the blob is created in the same origin context. Confirmed no issues.

6. Built-in example execution via direct URL import (IDE._loadExample): when examples/ is reachable as static files, import(url) and fetch(url) both work normally over HTTPS.

7. getUserMedia (webcam examples), AudioContext (audio-pulse, music-synth, solar-system audio), and File System Access API (showDirectoryPicker) all require a secure context (HTTPS or localhost). GitHub Pages serves exclusively over HTTPS, so all three APIs are available. getUserMedia additionally requires user-gesture gating (already done in examples). showDirectoryPicker is a nice-to-have for local dev and degrades gracefully (already guarded with window.showDirectoryPicker check at IDE.js:384).

8. HTTPS ensures no mixed-content issues with CDN resources.

## What Needs to Change

### 1. The examples/ directory MUST be moved under public/ or copied to dist/ (HIGH priority blocker)

This is the single largest structural gap. Currently the Vite dev server serves examples/ at /examples/... as static files. Vite's production build does NOT automatically copy directories that live outside public/. After vite build, dist/ will contain no examples/ subtree.

_loadExample (IDE.js:1304) does:
  const url = 
  mod = await import(url)    // dynamic ES module import
  fetch(url).then(r => r.text()) // source display in Monaco

Both calls will 404 on GitHub Pages unless examples/ is served. The fix: move examples/ into public/examples/ (or create a symlink). Vite copies public/ verbatim into dist/ without processing. This means:
- All 22 example directories (22 artlab.json manifests + .js entry files + assets) get copied as-is.
- The solar-system example uses new URL(, import.meta.url).href to resolve textures. This works correctly in the production build because import.meta.url points to the actual served URL. Texture assets under examples/solar-system/assets/textures/ will be served as static files (no Vite processing needed — they are JPEGs).
- Examples that import from src/ using relative paths like ../../src/stdlib/video.js (video-broadcast, video-fx, video-kaleidoscope, physics-particles) will BREAK in a public/ static deployment because Vite does not bundle them when copied verbatim. See item 3 below.

### 2. vite.config.js base URL must be set for non-root deployments (MEDIUM priority)

GitHub Pages typically serves a project site from https://<user>.github.io/<repo-name>/. Without base: '/<repo-name>/', Vite emits asset paths like /assets/index.js, which will 404 under a sub-path deployment.

Fix in vite.config.js:
  base: process.env.GITHUB_PAGES ? '/artlab/' : '/',

Or set it unconditionally if the repo name is fixed. This affects: all script/link tags in dist/index.html and dist/solar-system.html, all import() calls using Vite-resolved paths, and the Monaco/JSZip CDN constants (those are absolute HTTPS URLs and are not affected).

### 3. Examples that import from src/ stdlib need bundling (HIGH priority)

Four examples use relative paths that escape their own directory into src/:
- examples/video-broadcast/video-broadcast.js: import { webcam } from '../../src/stdlib/video.js'
- examples/video-fx/video-fx.js: import { webcam, captureCanvas } from '../../src/stdlib/video.js'
- examples/video-kaleidoscope/video-kaleidoscope.js: import { webcam } from '../../src/stdlib/video.js'
- examples/physics-particles/physics-particles.js: import { createParticleWorld, emitter, forceField } from '../../src/stdlib/physics/particles.js'

If examples/ is served as verbatim static files (via public/), these relative imports will resolve to paths outside the deployment root and will 404. Two options:
  a. Self-contain each example: inline the stdlib imports directly into the example file (increases duplication but makes each example fully standalone).
  b. Bundle each example with Vite: add each example entry to vite.config.js rollupOptions.input and emit as separate bundles. The bundled output in dist/ would have no cross-directory imports.
  c. Serve stdlib at a well-known public path (e.g. /artlab/stdlib/video.js) and rewrite the import paths to use the deployment base URL.
Option (b) is cleanest for long-term maintenance and lets Vite handle tree-shaking.

### 4. Solar-system example: texture assets work correctly via import.meta.url (no change needed)

The assetURL() helper in solar-system.js uses new URL('./assets/textures/', import.meta.url).href. This resolves relative to the module's actual URL at runtime, so textures in examples/solar-system/assets/textures/ will be found correctly as long as the directory structure is preserved under public/ (which the verbatim copy does). No change needed here.

### 5. GitHub Actions CI/CD workflow (LOW priority, one-time setup)

A GitHub Actions workflow is needed to automate deployment. The workflow should:
  1. Run npm ci
  2. Run npm run build (with GITHUB_PAGES=true or vite --base=/artlab/)
  3. Deploy dist/ to the gh-pages branch using actions/deploy-pages or peaceiris/actions-gh-pages

This is boilerplate and takes under 30 minutes to write.

## Blockers / Open Questions

1. Examples importing from src/: Must decide between inlining stdlib into each example or bundling examples through Vite. This affects 4 of 22 examples. Bundling through Vite is the recommended path.

2. Repo name / base URL: GitHub Pages deployment URL depends on the repository name (artlab vs artlab-ide etc.). The base URL in vite.config.js must match. If the site is served from a custom domain at the root, base: '/' works without changes.

3. Monaco web workers: Monaco spawns editor workers (TypeScript worker, JSON worker) using the CDN base URL. These workers are cross-origin (from cdn.jsdelivr.net). Cross-origin workers require the page to serve Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy and Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy headers, OR Monaco must be configured to use workerFactory with inline workers. GitHub Pages does not support custom HTTP response headers. This is a potential showstopper for Monaco TypeScript intellisense. Mitigations: (a) Disable TS workers (intellisense degrades but editor still works), (b) bundle Monaco locally (large: ~15 MB), (c) use a CDN that supports COOP/COEP (unpkg does not; jsdelivr does not). Research needed before committing to approach.

4. Rapier3D (@dimforge/rapier3d-compat): ships a WebAssembly binary. Vite should bundle it correctly into dist/assets/. No special handling needed for GitHub Pages beyond confirming wasm MIME type is served as application/wasm (GitHub Pages serves .wasm files correctly).

## Rough Effort Estimate

- Move examples/ into public/examples/ and verify 18 of 22 examples work: 1-2 hours
- Set base URL in vite.config.js and add GitHub Actions workflow: 1 hour
- Research and resolve Monaco web-worker COOP/COEP issue (blocker): 2-4 hours
- Bundle the 4 src/-dependent examples through Vite: 2-3 hours
- End-to-end QA on a test GitHub Pages deployment: 2-4 hours

Total: approximately 1-2 days of focused engineering work, assuming the Monaco worker issue has a tractable solution. If Monaco workers require bundling the editor locally, add another half-day for that migration.
title: Investigation: self-contained GitHub Pages deployment
